gz5_castlead.topic: Operation Cast Lead 2008–2009 and the Goldstone report

claims.text: An Egyptian-brokered six-month lull took effect on 19 June 2008; on 4 November 2008 Israel raided Deir al-Balah to destroy a tunnel, calling it a preemptive strike against plans to abduct soldiers; Hamas called it a ceasefire violation and responded with rockets.

Israel launched Operation Cast Lead on 27 December 2008 with the stated aim of stopping rocket fire; the ground invasion began on 3 January 2009; Israel declared a unilateral ceasefire on 18 January, Hamas a one-week ceasefire twelve hours later; withdrawal completed 21 January.
Palestinian deaths by source: PCHR 1,417; Al Mezan 1,409; B'Tselem 1,391; Gaza Health Ministry 1,440; IDF 1,166. Israeli deaths: 13, of them 10 soldiers (4 by friendly fire) and 3 civilians.

B'Tselem's breakdown: 773 of those killed did not take part in hostilities, 320 minors, 109 women, 245 police, 330 combatants; the IDF's March 2009 figures: 1,166 killed, 709 involved in hostilities, 295 unarmed civilians, 162 undetermined.
The UN fact-finding mission (Goldstone report, September 2009) accused both Palestinian militants and the Israeli army of war crimes and possible crimes against humanity.

On 1 April 2011 Goldstone wrote 'If I had known then what I know now, the Goldstone Report would have been a different document', concluding Israel did not target civilians as a matter of policy, and that Hamas's crimes were intentional.
The other three mission members, Hina Jilani, Christine Chinkin and Desmond Travers, said on 14 April 2011 'there is no justification for any demand or expectation for reconsideration of the report'.

On 18 December 2008 Hamas declared the truce over and refused to renew it, saying Israel 'did not abide by its obligations'; the Carter Center found that despite a 97% drop in attacks the truce 'did not do much to ease the siege of Gaza'.
Netanyahu said Goldstone's reversal 'must lead to the shelving of this report once and for all'; Goldstone cited Israel's own investigations for his revised conclusion on intentional targeting.

gz5_2012_2014.topic: Pillar of Defense 2012 and Protective Edge 2014

claims.text: Operation Pillar of Defense ran 14–21 November 2012, beginning with the airstrike that killed Hamas military chief Ahmed Jabari; Israel cited over 100 rockets in 24 hours and attacks on soldiers, with the stated aim 'to halt rocket attacks against civilian targets originating from the Gaza Strip'.

The UN High Commissioner counted 174 Palestinians killed, 107 of them civilians; B'Tselem 167, 62 of whom took part in hostilities; six Israelis were killed (four civilians, two soldiers); over 1,456 rockets were fired into Israel and about 421 intercepted by Iron Dome.

The Egyptian-brokered ceasefire of 21 November 2012 required Israel to stop hostilities 'including incursions and targeting of individuals' and the factions to stop rocket attacks, and provided for opening crossings; the fishing limit was raised to 6 nautical miles and cut back to 3 after 22 March 2013.

Three Israeli teenagers abducted 12 June 2014 were found dead on 30 June; Israel blamed Hamas, 'No evidence of Hamas involvement was offered by Israeli authorities at the time', and Khaled Meshaal later acknowledged Hamas members were responsible; Israel's West Bank operation killed about 11 Palestinians and arrested 350–600; a Palestinian teenager, Mohammed Abu Khdeir, was murdered in revenge.

The 2014 war began with Israeli air operations on 8 July, with the stated aim of stopping rocket fire, and a ground invasion 17 July–5 August with the stated aim of destroying tunnels; an open-ended ceasefire took effect 26 August.

OCHA counted 2,220 Palestinians killed, 1,492 of them civilians; the UN HRC 2,251 with 1,462 civilians; Israel's MFA 2,125 with about 36% civilians; 67 Israeli soldiers and six civilians in Israel were killed; the IDF counted 4,564 rockets and mortars fired; more than 7,000 homes were razed and about 89,000 damaged; OCHA estimated up to 520,000 displaced.

The UN Commission of Inquiry chaired by Mary McGowan Davis (22 June 2015) found 'substantial information pointing to the possible commission of war crimes by both Israel and Palestinian armed groups': 1,462 Palestinian civilians killed, a third of them children; 142 families lost three or more members in attacks on residential buildings (742 deaths); Palestinian groups fired 4,881 rockets and 1,753 mortars that 'appeared to have the intention of spreading terror among civilians'; six civilians in Israel killed; Israel did not respond to the commission's requests for access.

Israel struck targets in Gaza on 4–6 July 2014; on 7 July a Khan Yunis tunnel explosion killed seven Hamas militants (an Israeli strike per Hamas, the BBC and a senior IDF official; Hamas's own munitions per the IDF).
Of the 2014 Israeli dead, one of the six civilians was a Thai worker; most soldiers were killed in Gaza.
In 2012 Palestinian armed groups cited the blockade and the occupation of the West Bank including East Jerusalem.

In June 2015 Israel published its own report on the 2014 war, saying the military 'did the utmost to avoid civilian casualties' and blaming Hamas for firing from residential areas; Netanyahu said 'Whoever wants a baseless, automatic accusation against Israel can waste their time reading the UN report'.

gz5_march_2021.topic: The 2018 protests and the May 2021 war

claims.text: The UN Commission on the 2018 protests (30 March–31 December 2018) found 189 Palestinians killed, 183 by live ammunition, 35 children, 2 marked journalists and 3 marked paramedics; 6,106 injured by live ammunition; one Israeli soldier killed outside the protest sites and four injured at them.

The Commission found the demonstrations 'civilian in nature, with clearly stated political aims', found reasonable grounds to believe snipers shot journalists, health workers, children and people with disabilities 'knowing they were clearly recognizable as such', and said violations 'may constitute war crimes or crimes against humanity'; it also found Hamas 'failed to prevent' incendiary kites and balloons that caused fear and damage in southern Israel.

Acting foreign minister Yisrael Katz said 'Israel totally rejects the report', called it 'hostile, false and incorrect', and said 'Whoever pushes the residents of Gaza to the fences, including women and children, is the Hamas organization'; Israel refused to take part in the inquiry.

In May 2021, after protests over anticipated evictions in Sheikh Jarrah and police raids on the al-Aqsa compound on 7 and 10 May, Hamas demanded Israel remove police from the Temple Mount and Sheikh Jarrah by 6 p.m. on 10 May and then fired rockets; fighting lasted until an Egyptian-mediated ceasefire on 21 May.

In May 2021 at least 256 Palestinians were killed in Gaza including 66 children (UN), with HRW and the UN putting civilians at 129 of 260; at least 13 people were killed in Israel, including two children; about 4,360 rockets were fired, about 680 landing in Gaza, with Iron Dome interception at about 95 percent; on 15 May Israel destroyed the al-Jalaa building housing Al Jazeera and AP; OCHA counted 258 buildings destroyed.

The UN commission acknowledged 'some acts of significant violence' by demonstrators and that some were members of armed groups, but found those killed and injured were not directly participating in hostilities nor posing an imminent threat.

In May 2021 police said protesters threw stones and fireworks; Israel said it had killed 200 militants; the IDF said Hamas military intelligence was based in the al-Jalaa building, a claim AP asked it to prove; Iron Dome intercepted about 95% of rockets heading for populated areas.
